title: Linear MPC of a belt conveyor: horizon, constraints and comparison with PI
algorithm: Linear MPC (condensed QP, SciPy L-BFGS-B / SLSQP), offset-free via output disturbance estimate
plant_model: Single-mass belt with drive-force lag (RK4), model-based MPC on the linearisation

status.software: Executed from a clean kernel; local unit tests passed at build time; GitHub Actions has not been run on this repository

limitations: No terminal cost or set: no stability guarantee.
General-purpose SciPy solver; timing is for this machine only.
MPC model uses the true plant parameters (best case) except where a stale payload is stated.
PI and MPC tuned by different rules; compared on IAE against command variation.
Single input, single output, stable plant: no multivariable benefit tested.

checks.name: finite-horizon unconstrained first move equals the Riccati recursion (20 random states, N = 15)
MPC first-move gain error against the LQR gain falls with horizon (N = 2, 5, 10, 20)
MPC first-move gain at N = 40 equals the LQR gain within 1e-6 (relative)
box-constrained QP cost equals bounded least squares (BVLS) cost on 15 states, bounds active in most
checks.detail: max rel diff 2.9e-15, bounds active in 14/15

checks.name: rate-constrained QP satisfies the KKT conditions (non-negative multipliers, relative residual < 1e-4) and its limits to 1e-6
checks.detail: max relative KKT residual 1.2e-05, worst violation 3.5e-16

checks.name: rate-constrained QP cost is not above the trust-constr cost (interior-point, strictly feasible, stops short)
constraint-aware MPC has lower IAE than MPC that ignores the bounds (saturating step)
closed-loop IAE changes by less than 0.1% between N = 10 and N = 40 (gain has converged by N = 10)
slew-constrained MPC: command stays in [0, 1] and every step is within 0.05 (+1e-6)
with the slew limit, MPC has lower IAE than PI + external limiter
MPC with a stale payload model has zero steady-state error after the drop (offset-free)
MPC speed at the ceiling is within 1% of the closed-form maximum (30 kg)
no QP solve reported failure in any closed-loop run
mean QP solve time is below 10% of the sample time in every run (this machine, SciPy)
checks.detail: worst run mean 0.63 ms against 5 ms; single slowest solve 13.4 ms (not a check: timing outliers depend on the machine)
